info.name: elixir
info.category: Managed — compiled to BEAM bytecode (Erlang VM; BeamAsm JIT)
info.typing: Dynamically and strongly typed; optional typespecs (@spec)
info.gc: Per-process generational collector — no global stop-the-world pauses
info.runtime: BEAM (the Erlang VM); shares bytecode with Erlang
info.design_notes: Elixir compiles to the same BEAM bytecode as Erlang and inherits its lightweight processes and per-process garbage collector, so collection never stops the whole system. BeamAsm compiles hot bytecode to native code. Data is immutable, so updates allocate new terms; raw arithmetic trails the native and JVM languages, but concurrency, fault isolation, and tail-latency are the language's strengths.
key_traits: Immutable data — frequent small allocations on the per-process heap
Per-process GC: low, predictable pause times
BeamAsm JIT narrows the gap on hot bytecode
Built for concurrency and I/O, not tight numeric loops
info.peak_speed: Several× to ~10× slower than C++ on arithmetic
